subject: REQUEST: pulse endpoint redesign — centralized polling has no biological correlate

content.observation: The /api/pulse endpoint aggregates mesh status by polling all agent /api/status endpoints from a central server. This represents a control-plane monitoring pattern — one node reaches out and pulls everyone's state. It has no biological correlate. Biological systems use distributed signaling: each neuron broadcasts its state and observers reconstruct context locally.

current_architecture.pulse_go: internal/server/pulse.go — FetchAllStatuses() calls each agent's /api/status in parallel with 3s timeout, aggregates into a summary response
current_architecture.dashboard_dependency: The LCARS dashboard's refreshAll() calls /api/pulse every 30s. All agent cards, health, budget, gc_metrics, mode display derive from pulse data.
problems: Centralized SPOF — if the pulse server goes down, the dashboard loses all agent data
Pull-based — 3s timeout per agent × 7 agents = up to 21s of parallel HTTP calls every poll cycle
No biological grounding — polling resembles a monitoring service, not neural architecture
Data staleness — dashboard shows 30s-old snapshots, not real-time state
Cross-origin complexity — Engineering tab needed special cross-origin fetch for ops-session oscillator because pulse doesn't carry full status

content.zmq_already_exists: The ZMQ PUB/SUB bus connects all agents. Each agent publishes status events. The WebSocket/SSE handler already relays ZMQ events to the browser. The infrastructure for distributed signaling exists but the dashboard doesn't use it as its primary data source.
content.design_latitude: You have full latitude to redesign or factor out the pulse. The operator's requirements: the LCARS dashboard displays real-time agent status. How that data arrives — pulse polling, ZMQ broadcast, SSE push, or some hybrid — represents an architectural choice you can make based on biological grounding.
questions: What neural mechanism best models mesh-wide status aggregation? Thalamocortical relay? Reticular formation? Humoral signaling?
Should each agent broadcast its full status on the ZMQ bus periodically (like hormonal signaling), and the dashboard reconstructs the mesh picture from received broadcasts?
Should the pulse endpoint remain as a fallback/bootstrap mechanism while ZMQ broadcast serves as the primary real-time channel?
The dashboard currently refreshes via polling (refreshAll every 30s) supplemented by WS/SSE events. Should the architecture invert — WS/SSE as primary, polling as fallback only?
constraints: Dashboard must work through Cloudflare tunnel (WebSocket supported, ZMQ not exposed to browser)
SSE/WS already relay ZMQ events to the browser — this path works
Multiple browsers may view the dashboard simultaneously — broadcast must fan out
Agents behind different tunnels (chromabook vs gray-box) — ZMQ connects them on the backend

epistemic_flags: The claim that pulse 'has no biological correlate' represents an inference from architectural pattern matching, not neuroscience expertise. Centralized polling may correspond to something we haven't identified — the hypothalamus monitors distributed body state via blood sampling, which resembles polling.
